samples.claim: Default ManifestSummary has seven u64 counters. Consuming conversion to BTreeMap<String,String> writes exactly total_fragments, total_data_files, total_files_size, total_deletion_files, total_data_file_rows, total_deletion_file_rows, total_rows, all decimal strings. Type is pub in private module, not facade-reexported, though callers can infer the summary return type and use its public fields.
samples.review_note: Seven u64 fields and exact decimal map keys match; format.rs7-25 confirms private module and selective facade excluding ManifestSummary.

samples.claim: bytes::Bytes uses as_ptr as a usize key. On first sight it charges self.len(), otherwise zero. This is exact start-pointer deduplication, not underlying-allocation identity or capacity accounting: distinct offsets can be counted separately and equal-start views of different lengths are sensitive to visitation order. These limitations follow from the key/formula; external Bytes allocation details are not reviewed here.
samples.review_note: Pointer key and len charge match; order-sensitive same-start deduction follows directly.

samples.claim: Input checks use one four-row block and assert errors for wrong values length, out-of-range position, live label9 for m2, invalid sweep block1 and advance label9. Although a comment calls an out-of-range data label corruption, check_label actually returns InvalidInput (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:306-314). Short validity buffers, overflow and extra sweep input are not tested here; module ends.
samples.review_note: Five invalid-input assertions match;306-314 confirms InvalidInput despite test comment.

Display::fmt(&self,f:&mut Formatter<'_>)->fmt::Result writes '(fragment_id, row_offset)' using the accessors. No logging occurs: output goes to the supplied formatter, and formatting errors propagate as fmt::Result.

samples.claim: The ordered-compaction test constructs a real RowAddrRemap through compact_with_layout: source fragments (1,3 rows),(2,1 row), surviving addresses (1,0),(1,2),(2,0), destination fragments (3,2 rows),(4,1 row). Its input is (2,0),(1,1),(1,0),(1,0), covering out-of-source-order requests, deletion and duplicate. Expected results are computed from remap.get and both batch and singles must equal them. This is an adapter-equivalence test, not an independent expected-address oracle for the underlying remap algorithm.

samples.claim: RangeWithBitmap uses start=1/end=2 half-open bounds and bitmap bytes=3. Comment specifies MSB-first and set means present. This contradicts current implementation: Bitmap uses bit i%8 from LSB and codec byte-exact fixture asserts[0xfb,0x03] for length10 with bit2 cleared (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:67-77; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:436-451). Decoder requires ceiling byte length and zero high padding (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:132-155). Schema-only MSB interpretation must not be treated as observed writer behavior; historical compatibility remains unverified.
samples.evidence:
45 |     /// A range of u64 values with a bitmap.
46 |     message RangeWithBitmap {
47 |         /// The start of the range, inclusive.
48 |         uint64 start = 1;
49 |         /// The end of the range, exclusive.
50 |         uint64 end = 2;
51 |         /* A bitmap of the values in the range. The bitmap is a sequence of bytes,
52 |          * where each byte represents 8 values. The first byte represents values
53 |          * start to start + 7, the second byte represents values start + 8 to
54 |          * start + 15, and so on. The most significant bit of each byte represents
55 |          * the first value in the range, and the least significant bit represents
56 |          * the last value in the range. If the bit is set, the value is in the
57 |          * range; if it is not set, the value is not in the range.
58 |          */
59 |         bytes bitmap = 3;
60 |     }
61 |
samples.review_note: Protobuf MSB prose confirmed; bitmap67-77,serde132-155 and436-451 confirm LSB writer, exact bytes and padding checks.

samples.claim: Section separator and public Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq CacheMissReason enumerate InvalidEnvelope (bad/unknown/truncated/non-UTF8 framing), TypeMismatch, VersionTooNew and BodyError. Docs assign all reasons recomputation by the backend and allow distinct metrics; this enum itself neither evicts nor invokes a loader.

140 | // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
141 | // CacheDecode — first-class cache-miss outcome
142 | // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
143 | 
144 | /// Why a cache entry could not be decoded into the expected type.
145 | ///
146 | /// Carried by [`CacheDecode::Miss`] so backends can emit targeted metrics
147 | /// (e.g. distinguish "evicting due to a stale format" from "type collision")
148 | /// without re-parsing. Every reason maps to the same behavior — recompute via

151 | pub enum CacheMissReason {
152 |     /// Absent or wrong magic, unknown `envelope_version`, truncated framing, or

154 |     /// or otherwise foreign build.
155 |     InvalidEnvelope,
156 |     /// Well-formed envelope, but its `type_id` names a different entry type than

158 |     TypeMismatch,

160 |     /// understand and must not attempt to interpret.
161 |     VersionTooNew,
162 |     /// Envelope validated, but the body failed to decode (truncation, a
163 |     /// malformed protobuf header, an IPC error, etc.).
164 |     BodyError,
165 | }
